priced_in_summary: Not TOO_LATE, for the same reason it is not INVESTABLE: what has re-rated over the past year is the Power Systems / data-center-genset story (Total segment sales +19.38% in Q2 2026 alone), not the specific minor-NSR-permits-driven aftertreatment content this placement's thesis is actually about. Emission Solutions, the line this dive is chartered to evaluate, grew only 5.60% year over year in H1 2026, slower than the company as a whole. A TOO_LATE call requires the decomposition to show THIS occurrence's runway already spent; instead the multiple expansion visible in the stock (EV/operating income roughly 24.2x to 31.76x over the past year) is riding a different, larger, already richly-covered narrative that this dive's placement only partially and mechanically touches (the chain's own capture_inputs.shared_bom note already flags that CAT and CMI's aftertreatment content is 'the same revenue being described twice by stage' as their genset sales at position 5, meaning it cannot be bought separately from the broader story). What the price does ask, on the market's own 5-year reverse-DCF convention, is a 33.79% FCF CAGR against a company-wide like-for-like build this dive can defend at roughly 6.4%-9.3%, a gap that survives the cash-conversion stress this analyst's log has flagged as the most volatile input on prior names, though it narrows into the file's own 15.06pp horizon-spread noise band at the market's gentler 10-year convention. Combined with a heavily-covered, analyst-favored large-cap stock riding a link the chain's own heat block scored UNDISCOVERED before Cummins even had a market file on disk, and a real, resolved but material governance scar in exactly this discipline (the largest Clean Air Act civil penalty in history, for admitted emissions-defeat devices), the honest verdict is WATCH: a real, well-financed growth story, priced for a bigger and different acceleration than the specific link this dive is scored on can defend.

Cummins is disclosed-capacity-constrained on its largest gensets: a $150 million expansion of its Fridley, Minnesota facility, announced February 2026, aims to boost QSK95 output 30% to address 18-month lead times, direct evidence the underlying demand this content rides along with is real and currently supply-constrained rather than speculative.

bear.point: Cummins' own emissions-compliance history carries the largest civil penalty in Clean Air Act history: a $1.675 billion federal penalty plus a $372 million California settlement (roughly $2 billion total, agreed December 2023, finalized 2024) for admittedly installing illegal defeat-device software on approximately 960,000 model-year 2013-2023 RAM 2500/3500 truck engines, a decade-long pattern rather than an isolated incident, in the exact discipline (emissions-control credibility) this placement's 'Emission Solutions' marketing depends on. Fully resolved, cash-settled and already reflected in FY2023-2024 financials (FY2023 operating income fell to $1,761M from $2,929M in FY2022 on the litigation accrual, and FY2024 operating cash flow fell to $1,487M as the cash penalty was paid), but a real integrity scar this dive weighs against the earnings-quality grade rather than treating as fully in the past.

Row 1 carries the solve as a labelled proxy under a stated flat-margin/flat-conversion assumption, and this dive additionally builds its own FCF-CAGR-equivalent (6.43%-9.32% at the 5-year convention, varying the cash-conversion assumption between the FY2025 ratio and the FY2022-2025 average rather than only declaring one) in net_gap_direction from its own revenue, margin and conversion assumptions, so the comparison that decides the verdict is like for like.

rows.market_implied_note: This is the solved 5-year FCF CAGR, not a decomposed revenue CAGR. Held here as the closest proxy under a flat-margin/flat-conversion assumption (if margin and cash conversion held at their FY2025 levels, revenue would also have to compound near this rate), and named as such.
rows.why: 7.5% sits above the achieved trailing three-year revenue CAGR (6.25%) but below the low end of the company's own twice-raised FY2026 guide (10-13%), because that guide describes one cyclical-high year driven by a data-center pull-forward and a recovering truck cycle, not a sustained five-year rate for a $33.7B diversified engine and power-systems maker whose four largest segments (Engine, Components, Distribution, Accelera) remain flat-to-cyclical. Below the 50th percentile of Cummins' own FY2018-2025 annual growth range deliberately, because the years that cleared 10%+ (2021, 2022, 2023) were each followed by a flat or down year (2024 +0.1%, 2025 -1.3%).
rows.structural_reason: Power Systems (data-center standby/prime power) is real, disclosed and capacity-constrained (bull[0]), but at 12.87% of Q2 2026 external sales it is a minority of consolidated revenue, so even strong double-digit growth in that one segment blends down to a high-single-digit company-wide rate once the other four segments are held near their own historical trend.
rows.leading_indicator: Q3 2026 consolidated net sales growth at or above 10% (watch_triggers[1]) and Power Systems' external-sales share of the total rising meaningfully above its 12.87% Q2 2026 level, both reportable 2026-11-02.

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose a margin path from the headline FCF CAGR. Recorded NULL rather than invented.
rows.why: 13.0% is a genuine step up from the FY2025 print (11.95%), defended on a real mix shift already visible in the disclosed segment data: Power Systems posted a 24.5% EBITDA margin in Q2 2026 (up from 22.8% in Q2 2025) while Engine and Components margins actually compressed year over year (12.5% vs 13.8%, 13.2% vs 14.7%), attributed by the company itself to 'higher incentive compensation, tied to expected record full year results' rather than a structural cost problem. 13.0% assumes the Power-Systems-led mix shift outweighs that transient headwind once it laps, not that every segment expands together.
rows.structural_reason: A widening EBITDA-margin gap between Power Systems (24.5%) and the rest of the portfolio (12.5%-13.6%), combined with Power Systems' rising revenue share, mechanically lifts the consolidated blend even if no individual segment's own margin improves further.
rows.leading_indicator: Segment EBITDA margins at the Q3 2026 release: Power Systems holding at or above its Q2 2026 level (24.5%) while Engine/Components margins stop compressing once the incentive-compensation comparison laps, reportable 2026-11-02.

rows.market_implied_note: The filed solve does not decompose a reinvestment return, and no company-disclosed ROIC or ROCE figure appears in any source read this run. Recorded NULL rather than invented.
rows.why: A crude proxy, not a disclosed figure: incremental operating income from FY2022 to FY2025 ($4,025M less $2,929M = $1,096M) over cumulative FY2023-2025 capital expenditure ($1,213M + $1,208M + $1,235M = $3,656M) gives approximately 30.0%. This is a rough incremental-margin-on-capex measure that ignores depreciation timing, working capital and lags, disclosed as a proxy rather than a rigorous ROIIC, and held at the high end of what this dive would defend rather than extrapolated further because the underlying capex step-up (from roughly $700-900M annually pre-2022 to $1.2B+ since) is itself named as the structural reason, not assumed to compound.
rows.structural_reason: The $150 million Fridley, Minnesota expansion (bull[0]) is a disclosed, dollar-figured example of capital going directly toward the capacity-constrained, higher-margin product (QSK95 large-bore engines) behind this dive's own margin and growth rows, rather than a diversified or defensive capex program.
rows.leading_indicator: FY2026 capital expenditure and operating income figures at the FY2026 release, against this dive's own $3,656M three-year cumulative capex and $1,096M three-year incremental operating income base.

rows.why: No disagreement, and saying so is worth a row. 2.5% perpetual growth is a reasonable long-run nominal assumption for a diversified global industrial (method section 7's own base-rate ceiling, roughly long-run nominal GDP), and this dive would not move it. The assumption this dive would question is not the terminal rate but the discount rate: 9% is not obviously wrong for a US industrial with sub-1x net-debt-to-EBITDA leverage (0.6936x), but the file publishes no sensitivity to it beyond the horizon table, the same data-plane gap this analyst's log first named on ANDR.VI. Method section 7 forbids re-solving in session for the filed column itself, so this gap is named rather than filled.

rows.note: Built like for like rather than compared revenue against FCF, and the cash-conversion assumption is declared AND varied rather than only declared, per this analyst's own log's standing lesson from ANDR.VI and 688425.SS ('a declared convention is an untested one'). Revenue $33,670,000,000 compounding at 7.5% for five years gives $48,336,000,000 in FY2030; at a 13.0% steady-state operating margin that is operating income of $6,283,700,000 against $4,025,000,000 in FY2025. Converting to free cash flow two ways: holding FY2025's own cash-conversion ratio (free cash flow over operating income, $2,386,000,000 / $4,025,000,000 = 0.5928) gives FY2030 FCF of $3,724,900,000, a 9.32% FCF CAGR; reverting instead to the FY2022-2025 average ratio (four-year average FCF $1,616,000,000 over four-year average operating income $3,116,250,000 = 0.5186) gives FY2030 FCF of $3,258,400,000, a 6.43% FCF CAGR. Against the filed 5-year market-implied 33.79%, the gap is 24.47-27.36 percentage points depending on which conversion ratio is held, both far outside the file's own 15.06-point horizon_spread: a real gap either way. Against the filed 10-year market-implied 18.73% (holding the same 7.5%/13.0% assumptions out to ten years: FY2035 revenue $69,395,000,000, operating income $9,021,400,000, FCF $5,349,300,000 at the FY2025 ratio or $4,678,900,000 at the average ratio, giving FCF CAGRs of 8.41% and 6.96%), the gap narrows to 10.32-11.77 points, INSIDE the 15.06-point horizon_spread: not a demonstrated gap by the file's own rule at that convention. The sign does not flip between horizons (both say the market wants more than this dive defends), only the SIZE of the finding does, and this dive claims the 5-year reading as the operative one because that is the convention the filed solve defaults to and the one the would_buy_zone below is drawn against, consistent with this analyst's prior VRT/HUBB/MYRG/ESLT dives choosing the tougher convention. pre_mortem.prompt: It is 2027-09-06. This WATCH was wrong. What happened?
reasons: Power Systems' share of consolidated external sales kept widening past its 12.87% Q2 2026 level AND pulled the rest of the portfolio up with it via intersegment engine content, so consolidated growth cleared the guided 13% high end for multiple quarters running and Emission Solutions' own growth rate closed most of the gap to Power Systems' -- the 'decoupling' this dive found at dive time was a lag, not a structural split, and the market's whole-company extrapolation was closer to right than this dive's segment-level read.

A minor-NSR-permits-specific catalyst materialized (the chain's own S2 scenario: a state authority tightening its permit template, or a federal rule change raising presumptive best-available-control-technology standards) and forced an incremental content step-up per engine, re-accelerating Emission Solutions specifically and independent of the broader Power Systems story -- the exact mechanism this dive said was not yet visible in the disclosed growth rate became visible within the review window.

This dive's own 13.0% steady-state operating-margin assumption proved too conservative: the mix shift toward Power Systems (24.5% EBITDA margin against 12.5%-13.6% elsewhere) combined with operating leverage from capacity investment (the Fridley expansion) compounded faster than modeled, so the 'real' free-cash-flow growth rate underlying the business converged toward the market's ask rather than this dive's own 6.43%-9.32% build, meaning the price was closer to fair than this dive's own reverse-DCF comparison judged it to be.
pre_mortem.why_the_market_could_be_right: All three reasons name a mechanism under which the market's implicit whole-company extrapolation would turn out correct rather than an error: sustained segment-share widening with intersegment pull-through, a policy catalyst landing inside review_by rather than after it, or this dive's own margin assumption sitting below what capacity investment actually delivers. None of these is dismissed as impossible; watch_triggers[0] and [1] and the independence_test's falsification condition are built specifically to catch the first two before FY2027, and the earnings_quality grade B (not A) already flags that this dive is not treating Cummins' current-year clean mechanical inputs as a stronger endorsement than the compliance history and margin assumptions warrant.

red_team.surviving_bear_case: The verdict survives fresh-context attack because its three load-bearing legs each independently reproduce rather than merely restate: the specific product line this placement is chartered to evaluate, Emission Solutions, is disclosed-growing at 5.60% year over year in H1 2026, slower than the company as a whole (6.17%) and far slower than Power Systems (19.38%), the segment actually carrying the data-center re-rating, and the chain's own shared_bom note already ties this content to the same genset revenue counted at position 5, so it cannot be bought separately from that larger, already-priced story; the market's own 5-year reverse-DCF convention asks for a 33.79% free-cash-flow CAGR against a like-for-like build this dive defends at 6.43%-9.32%, a gap independently re-derived in this attack to within 0.01% of the filed enterprise value and confirmed in price space (55.6%-60.4% below spot) at either the 5-year or the gentler 10-year convention; and a stock that is heavily covered by sell-side analysts (18 analysts, consensus Buy, average target 35.5% above spot) is riding a chain link the chain's own heat block scored UNDISCOVERED before Cummins even had a market file on disk, a mismatch between the vehicle and the exposure this dive is meant to be scoring. The one gap this attack could not fully close, how much of Power Systems' growth specifically reaches Components' intersegment sales, does not weaken the finding: the intersegment channel that exists grew slower than Power Systems itself, which is consistent with the decoupling this dive found rather than a challenge to it.
